stem: Which factor helped drive European imperial expansion in the late nineteenth century?

options.text: Competition for raw materials and markets
A plan to end overseas trade
A common decision to dissolve empires
A rejection of industrial production

explanation: Industrial economies and strategic rivalry both shaped imperial expansion; no single motive explains every case.

stem: Which statement best describes the motives for nineteenth-century imperialism?

options.text: They were identical in every empire and colony
They varied and could include strategic, economic, political and missionary aims
They were limited to scientific research
They aimed only to abolish international trade

explanation: Imperial projects had multiple motives, and their relative importance varied by place and government.

stem: What did a protectorate generally allow an imperial power to do?

options.text: Transfer all political authority to an elected colonial parliament
End its influence over foreign relations
Exercise substantial control over a territory while retaining a local ruler or government
Create an equal alliance between independent states

explanation: A protectorate often preserved a local authority formally while giving the imperial power decisive influence, especially over external affairs.

stem: Which method was commonly used by European powers to claim authority in parts of Africa?

options.text: Elections supervised by the African Union
A continent-wide referendum organised by African states
A treaty signed by the League of Nations
Treaties negotiated with local rulers, later interpreted as claims of control

explanation: European powers often relied on treaties with African rulers, although the meanings and conditions of those agreements were frequently contested.

stem: Why did European powers build ports and railways in many colonies?

options.text: To support administration, military movement and the extraction or transport of goods
To prevent access to mines and plantations
To end all trade with Europe
To create a single African parliament

explanation: Colonial transport links commonly served administration and commercial extraction, though their uses varied by region.

stem: Which distinction between a colony and a sphere of influence is most accurate?

options.text: A sphere of influence always meant complete independence
A colony involved direct territorial rule; a sphere could involve strong influence without formal annexation
A colony was governed by the League of Nations
The terms had identical legal meanings

explanation: Formal colonial rule and informal influence were different arrangements, though both could limit local sovereignty.

stem: When and where did the West Africa Conference, commonly called the Berlin Conference, meet?

options.text: Paris, from 1870 to 1871
Vienna, from 1814 to 1815
Berlin, from 1884 to 1885
Brussels, from 1900 to 1901

explanation: The conference met in Berlin from November 1884 to February 1885.

stem: Which German chancellor hosted the Berlin Conference?

options.text: Helmuth von Moltke
Wilhelm II
Friedrich Ebert
Otto von Bismarck

explanation: Bismarck convened the conference as German chancellor.

stem: Which statement about African participation at the Berlin Conference is correct?

options.text: African rulers and representatives were not invited as negotiating parties
African states chaired every session
The conference was an assembly elected across Africa
Only African rulers could sign the General Act

explanation: The conference was conducted by foreign powers; African societies whose territories were affected had no representation as parties to its negotiations.

stem: What was one purpose of the General Act of the Berlin Conference?

options.text: Create a legislature for all African territories
Set rules among European powers concerning trade, navigation and claims in parts of Africa
Immediately draw every present-day African border
Grant independence to all African states

explanation: The Act addressed principles for European claims and navigation; it did not itself settle every later boundary.

stem: What did the General Act provide regarding navigation on the Congo River?

options.text: Exclusive control for Portugal
A ban on commercial vessels
Freedom of navigation for the contracting powers under the Act
Transfer of the river to the United States

explanation: The Act included provisions for free navigation on the Congo, alongside provisions for trade and the basin.

stem: What did the Berlin Act provide regarding the Niger River?

options.text: The river was closed to all foreign trade
The river was placed under Belgian rule
Its course became the border of every West African colony
Navigation was to be free for the contracting powers under the Act

explanation: The General Act included a separate navigation regime for the Niger; it was not a map of all later colonial boundaries.

stem: Who was recognised as sovereign of the Congo Free State in 1885?

options.text: Leopold II of Belgium
Napoleon III of France
Bismarck of Germany
Cecil Rhodes of Britain

explanation: The International Association of the Congo transferred authority to Leopold II, who became sovereign of the Congo Free State.

stem: Which organisation preceded recognition of the Congo Free State under Leopold II?

options.text: Young Italy
International Association of the Congo
German East Africa Company
League of Nations Secretariat

explanation: The International Association of the Congo negotiated claims and treaties before the Congo Free State was recognised under Leopold II.

stem: Which European power ruled German East Africa before the First World War?

options.text: Belgium
Italy
Germany
Portugal

explanation: German East Africa was a German colony before the First World War; after the war its territories were redistributed under mandates.

stem: Which pair of powers held major rival claims in the Congo basin during the Berlin Conference era?

options.text: Japan and the United States
Italy and Greece
Austria-Hungary and Serbia
France and the International Association of the Congo

explanation: Diplomatic records from the period discuss the competing claims of France and the International Association of the Congo, alongside other European interests.

stem: What political status did the Congo territory receive in 1885 under Leopold II?

options.text: The Congo Free State, ruled as Leopold II’s personal state
A Belgian parliamentary province from the outset
An independent republic elected by Congolese voters
A French protectorate

explanation: In 1885 the Congo Free State was recognised under Leopold II; Belgium annexed it as the Belgian Congo in 1908.

stem: When did Belgium take direct control of the Congo from Leopold II?
explanation: Belgium annexed the Congo Free State in 1908, ending Leopold II’s personal rule there.

stem: What helped prompt international criticism of Leopold II’s rule in the Congo?

options.text: The creation of an elected Congolese parliament
The abolition of rubber production
Reports of coercive extraction and abuses under the concession system
The Congo’s refusal to trade with Europe

explanation: Reports and investigations exposed severe abuses and coercive extraction, contributing to reform pressure and Belgium’s annexation of the territory.

stem: Which resource became central to the Congo concession system during Leopold II’s rule?

options.text: Coal
Wool
Tea
Rubber

explanation: Rubber extraction became a major feature of the Congo concession system, alongside ivory and other commercial interests.

stem: Which statement best describes the Congo Reform movement?

options.text: It campaigned against abuses in the Congo Free State and helped build pressure for change
It sought to restore the Berlin Conference
It created the Congo Free State under Leopold II
It promoted the annexation of Belgium by France

explanation: The reform campaign publicised abuses in the Congo Free State and helped increase pressure for Belgian takeover.

stem: Which change followed Belgium’s annexation of the Congo in 1908?

options.text: The Congo became an independent republic immediately
The territory became the Belgian Congo under Belgian state rule
Leopold II resumed personal sovereignty
The territory joined German East Africa

explanation: After 1908 the Belgian state governed the colony as the Belgian Congo, replacing Leopold II’s personal state.

stem: What did the Berlin Conference establish about claims along parts of the African coast?

options.text: Every African kingdom became a signatory
All coastal territories were declared independent
Powers were to notify other signatories of new coastal possessions or protectorates
The conference prohibited any future treaty with local rulers

explanation: The General Act established notification procedures for new coastal possessions and protectorates among its signatories.

stem: Which statement best distinguishes the Berlin Conference from the later Scramble for Africa?

options.text: The conference completed every conquest before it opened
The conference was an African independence congress
The conference ended European competition for overseas territories
The conference set diplomatic rules among powers; territorial occupations and agreements continued afterward

explanation: The conference shaped rules used by European powers, but subsequent bilateral agreements and occupations continued the partition process.

stem: Which event occurred first?

options.text: Berlin Conference opened in 1884
Congo Free State annexed by Belgium in 1908
Maji Maji uprising began in 1905
Battle of Adwa was fought in 1896

explanation: The Berlin Conference opened in 1884, before the other listed events.

stem: Which sequence correctly orders these events?

options.text: Battle of Adwa → Berlin Conference → Maji Maji uprising
Berlin Conference (1884–85) → Battle of Adwa (1896) → Maji Maji uprising (1905–07)
Maji Maji uprising → Battle of Adwa → Berlin Conference
Battle of Adwa → Maji Maji uprising → Berlin Conference

explanation: The conference preceded Adwa, and both occurred before the Maji Maji uprising.

stem: Which event came immediately before Belgium annexed the Congo in 1908?

options.text: The Berlin Conference in 1884–85
The Battle of Adwa in 1896
The Maji Maji uprising in German East Africa
The Boxer uprising in China in 1900

explanation: The Maji Maji uprising took place in 1905–07, shortly before Belgium annexed the Congo in 1908.

stem: In which year did Ethiopian forces defeat Italy at Adwa?
explanation: The Battle of Adwa took place on 1 March 1896.

stem: Which event took place in German East Africa in 1905–07?

options.text: The Maji Maji uprising
The Boxer uprising
The Battle of Adwa
The Berlin Conference

explanation: The Maji Maji uprising against German colonial rule took place from 1905 to 1907 in German East Africa.

stem: Which sequence is correctly ordered?

options.text: Adwa → Congo Free State recognised → Maji Maji uprising
Congo Free State recognised (1885) → Adwa (1896) → Belgium annexes Congo (1908)
Maji Maji uprising → Adwa → Congo Free State recognised
Belgium annexes Congo → Adwa → Berlin Conference

explanation: The Congo Free State was recognised in 1885, Ethiopia defeated Italy at Adwa in 1896, and Belgium annexed the Congo in 1908.

stem: Which country remained independent after defeating Italy at Adwa in 1896?

options.text: Eritrea
Somalia
Ethiopia
Libya

explanation: Ethiopia’s victory at Adwa preserved its independence against Italy’s attempted conquest.

stem: Which territory was recognised as a German colony in East Africa before 1914?

options.text: Belgian Congo
French West Africa
Italian Somaliland
German East Africa

explanation: German East Africa was a German colonial possession before the First World War.

stem: Which state became a Belgian colony in 1908?

options.text: The Congo
Ethiopia
Morocco
Egypt

explanation: Belgium annexed the Congo Free State in 1908 and renamed it the Belgian Congo.

stem: Which description of European rule in Rwanda is accurate for the colonial period?

options.text: Italy ruled it continuously from 1885 to 1962
Germany ruled it before the First World War; Belgium administered it after the war
Portugal ruled it as part of Angola
France administered it under the League of Nations throughout the nineteenth century

explanation: Rwanda was part of German East Africa before the First World War and was later administered by Belgium under the postwar mandate system.

stem: Which river basin was central to the General Act’s provisions on trade and navigation?

options.text: The Rhine basin
The Danube basin
The Congo basin
The Amazon basin

explanation: The Berlin Act included provisions concerning commerce and navigation in the Congo basin.

stem: What did a European “sphere of influence” in China usually indicate?

options.text: China had become a single European colony
The League of Nations governed the region
All foreign powers had equal military control
A power claimed special political or economic privileges in a region without necessarily annexing all of China

explanation: In China, spheres of influence referred to special interests or privileges claimed by foreign powers, not a complete partition into formal colonies.

stem: Which African state defeated Italy at the Battle of Adwa?

options.text: Ethiopia
Asante
Sokoto
Zulu Kingdom

explanation: Ethiopian forces defeated the Italian army at Adwa in 1896.

stem: Which Ethiopian ruler led the country at the time of the Battle of Adwa?

options.text: Tewodros II
Menelik II
Haile Selassie
Yohannes IV

explanation: Menelik II was emperor of Ethiopia at the time of the 1896 victory at Adwa.

stem: Against which colonial power was the Maji Maji uprising directed?

options.text: Belgium
Portugal
Germany
Italy

explanation: The Maji Maji uprising challenged German colonial rule in German East Africa.

stem: Which description best fits the Maji Maji uprising?

options.text: A treaty conference in Berlin
A rebellion against Dutch rule in Indonesia
An Italian campaign against Ethiopia
A broad revolt against German colonial rule involving multiple communities in German East Africa

explanation: The uprising brought together different groups in resistance to German colonial rule, though its causes and course varied locally.

stem: What was the outcome of the Battle of Adwa?

options.text: Ethiopia defeated Italy and preserved its independence
Italy annexed Ethiopia and ended its monarchy
Germany took control of Ethiopia
The battle created the Congo Free State

explanation: The Ethiopian victory at Adwa in 1896 halted Italy’s attempt to conquer the country at that time.

stem: Which statement best compares African responses to European expansion?

options.text: All African rulers responded in the same way
Responses ranged from military resistance and diplomacy to negotiated arrangements; outcomes differed by region
Every state was conquered immediately after the Berlin Conference
African societies had no political institutions before European rule

explanation: African polities used different strategies and experienced different outcomes; the partition was not a single event or uniform process.

stem: Which event helped open several Chinese ports to foreign trade in the nineteenth century?

options.text: The Austro-Prussian War
The Congress of Berlin
The Opium Wars and the treaties that followed
The Franco-Prussian War

explanation: The treaties following the Opium Wars opened ports and granted foreign powers commercial privileges in China.

stem: What was one purpose of the 1899–1900 Open Door Notes on China?

options.text: Transfer China to British colonial rule
End all foreign commerce in Chinese ports
Create a Chinese parliament under European control
Promote equal trading opportunity among foreign powers in China

explanation: John Hay’s Open Door Notes sought equal commercial access among powers operating in China while affirming its territorial integrity.

stem: Who issued the Open Door Notes concerning China in 1899?

options.text: U.S. Secretary of State John Hay
British Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli
German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck
French Emperor Napoleon III

explanation: John Hay sent the first Open Door Note in September 1899 to powers with interests in China.

stem: What was the Boxer uprising directed against in China?

options.text: The German Zollverein
Foreign influence and Christian missionary activity, among other targets
The Ottoman administration in the Balkans
The British government in India alone

explanation: The Boxer movement opposed foreign influence and missionary activity; its causes and participants were varied.

stem: Which power ruled the Dutch East Indies during the imperial era?

options.text: France
Belgium
The Netherlands
Germany

explanation: The Netherlands governed the Dutch East Indies, centred on the Indonesian archipelago.

stem: Which statement about the Open Door policy is accurate?

options.text: It immediately ended every foreign privilege in China
It made China a colony of the United States
It required China to join the German Empire
It sought equal commercial opportunity in China while foreign powers retained existing spheres and privileges

explanation: The policy advocated equal trade access but did not immediately remove existing foreign spheres, leased territories or privileges.

stem: Which comparison between the Congo Free State and Ethiopia in the late nineteenth century is accurate?

options.text: The Congo came under Leopold II’s rule, while Ethiopia defeated Italy at Adwa and remained independent
Both were ruled by Leopold II
Both were annexed by Belgium in 1908
Ethiopia was a German protectorate after Adwa

explanation: Leopold II ruled the Congo Free State, whereas Ethiopia’s victory over Italy at Adwa preserved its independence at that time.

stem: Which comparison between the Berlin Conference and the Congress of Berlin is correct?

options.text: Both meetings were held in 1878 to divide China
The 1884–85 conference set rules relating to African claims; the 1878 congress revised Balkan arrangements
Both were African independence congresses
The 1878 congress created the Congo Free State

explanation: The Berlin Conference of 1884–85 concerned Africa, while the Congress of Berlin of 1878 revised the postwar settlement in the Balkans.

stem: Which comparison between formal annexation and a sphere of influence is accurate?

options.text: Both always create fully independent states
A sphere of influence is always more direct than annexation
Annexation transfers territory to direct rule; a sphere of influence may leave formal sovereignty while granting special privileges
Annexation applies only to trade and never to territory

explanation: Annexation and spheres of influence describe different forms of control, although both could constrain the affected society’s sovereignty.

stem: Which comparison between European imperialism in Africa and China is most accurate?

options.text: China was divided into the same formal colonies as Africa
European powers exercised no influence in China
Every African territory remained independent after 1900
Many African territories came under formal colonial rule, while China retained a government but faced foreign privileges and spheres of influence

explanation: Imperial control took different forms: formal colonial rule was widespread in Africa, while foreign powers also claimed privileges and spheres in China.

stem: Which statement best compares the Berlin Act and the Open Door policy?

options.text: The Act regulated navigation and claims among signatories in parts of Africa; the Open Door Notes addressed equal commercial access in China
Both were treaties granting independence to all colonised peoples
The Act applied to China and the Open Door Notes to the Congo River
Both created the League of Nations

explanation: The Berlin Act addressed rules in the Congo and Niger regions; the Open Door Notes proposed equal trading opportunity in China.

stem: Which comparison between Adwa and the Maji Maji uprising is accurate?

options.text: Both were treaties signed at Berlin
Adwa was an Ethiopian victory over Italy; Maji Maji was a revolt against German colonial rule in East Africa
Adwa was a Chinese uprising and Maji Maji was an Italian conquest
Both resulted in the immediate end of European colonialism in Africa

explanation: Adwa preserved Ethiopian independence after victory over Italy; Maji Maji resisted German colonial rule but was suppressed.

stem: What was one long-term effect of colonial boundaries drawn without local consent?

options.text: They ended all regional conflicts
They guaranteed equal political representation
They could divide communities or combine groups with different political histories
They prevented later nationalist movements

explanation: Colonial boundary-making often disregarded existing political and social arrangements, contributing to later disputes and political challenges.

stem: Which change commonly accompanied colonial economic policies?

options.text: Colonies were barred from exporting raw materials
All local economies became industrialised at the same pace
Colonial governments ended all cash-crop production
Production and transport were often organised to serve imperial extraction and trade

explanation: Colonial economies were frequently reorganised around extraction and export, though patterns differed by colony.

stem: Which statement about the Berlin Conference’s role in African partition is most accurate?

options.text: It set diplomatic rules, while conquest and boundary agreements continued afterward
It drew every modern African border in one session
It created independent African states under one constitution
It ended all European claims to Africa

explanation: The conference did not complete the partition; powers continued to occupy territory and negotiate boundaries afterward.

stem: Which conclusion best reflects the varied effects of imperialism?

options.text: All colonies experienced identical economic and political changes
Imperial rule reshaped political authority and economic systems, but effects differed among regions and societies
Imperial rule had no effect on local political institutions
Colonialism ended every form of local resistance

explanation: Imperialism changed political and economic structures in diverse ways; local conditions and forms of resistance produced varied outcomes.

stem: Which relationship between African resistance and imperial rule is supported by the historical record?

options.text: Resistance was absent from all African regions
Every uprising immediately expelled the imperial power
Resistance took different forms and sometimes delayed or defeated conquest, as at Adwa
The Berlin Conference ended local political agency

explanation: Adwa demonstrates that African resistance could defeat a colonial campaign; other struggles, such as Maji Maji, had different outcomes.

stem: Which summary best captures the Scramble for Africa and imperialism in Asia?

options.text: The Berlin Conference alone created every empire and fixed all borders
European imperialism affected only Africa and had no Asian dimension
Every imperial power used identical methods and faced no resistance
European expansion used varied political and economic controls; local societies responded differently, and neither conference agreements nor colonial maps captured every local reality

explanation: Imperial expansion varied by region and method; formal rule, spheres of influence, diplomacy, resistance and later boundary changes all shaped outcomes.
